title: Inspiration4 crew comprehensive metabolic panel, four crew members, seven timepoints (L-92 to R+194)
documentation: Overbey EG et al., 'Collection of biospecimens from the Inspiration4 mission establishes the standards for the Space Omics and Medical Atlas (SOMA)', Nature Communications 2024; data access described in https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11094041/
Timepoints: L = days before launch, R = days after return; the mission flew 15 to 18 September 2021 (three days)
mission: SpaceX Inspiration4 (commercial, three days in orbit, September 2021); subjects C001 to C004
instrument: CMP, 19 analytes (glucose, electrolytes, renal function, liver chemistry); clinical laboratory results submitted to OSDR (OSD-575, ALSDA organization, file subdirectory 'Original Submitted')
cadence: Seven blood draws per person: L-92, L-44, L-3, R+1, R+45, R+82, R+194 (no in-flight draw)

VALUE.description: Result in UNITS; 'NA' where not reported

RANGE_MIN.description: Laboratory reference range low, same unit

RANGE_MAX.description: Laboratory reference range high, same unit

UNITS.description: Unit as reported; UCUM mapping: mg/dL = mg/dL, mmol/L = mmol/L, g/dL = g/dL, U/L = U/L, mL/min/1.73m2 = mL/min/{1.73_m2}, (calc) = 1

timepoint.description: Timepoint relative to launch (L) or return (R), in days

preprocessing: None; the OSDR file LSDS-8_Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel_CMP.upload_SUBMITTED.csv saved as supplied and renamed to i4_osd575_cmp.csv.
license: NASA Open Science Data Repository, open-access file (the OSDR file listing marks it restricted: false). OSDR terms: https://science.nasa.gov/reference/osdr-help-terms-and-conditions/. US Government work. NASA material is generally not subject to copyright in the United States (NASA media usage guidelines, https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/). Credit NASA as the source; no NASA logo or insignia is used (NASA-SOURCES.md section 4).
provenance_note: REPLAY of real crew laboratory results, coded IDs only; never shown as a crew member of this product.
is_not: Not astronaut (NASA career) data: Inspiration4 was a commercial civilian crew on a three-day flight.
No in-flight sample, so it cannot show an in-flight trend; it shows a personal baseline before flight and the change after return.
Laboratory reference ranges are the lab's population ranges, not a personal usual value.

consumers.component: personal baselines (usual values) for laboratory indicators
consumers.use: Real per-person series: three preflight draws build each person's usual value for cbc, electrolytes, renal_function, liver_chemistry and glucose (input-dictionary.json); R+1 to R+194 test the deviation and return-to-baseline logic against real numbers.
Laboratory record entry with units and reference ranges as a lab reports them, including 'NA' cells that must stay missing (AGENTS rule 5).
